intervals.note: Evidence date, not a commissioning date: this is the earliest operation of the machine documented by a source fetched in this session (NuMI beam paper, MINOS data taking from 20 May 2005). The machine has run since the 1970s; no fetchable source gave its commissioning date (fnal.gov and history.fnal.gov returned HTTP 403).
intervals.quote: the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector

start.display: in operation by 2005; commissioning date not sourced

name: Fermilab Main Injector
notes: Design energy 150 GeV per the NuMI beam paper; 120 GeV is the neutrino-production operating point.

beam_energy.note: Operating energy for neutrino production; the design energy is 150 GeV.
beam_energy.quote: The NuMI beam is presently the world's most powerful neutrino beam and is produced by the 120 GeV protons extracted from the Fermilab Main Injector.

circumference.quote: The Recycler is a fixed energy machine of 8 GeV located on the top of the MI with the same circumference of 3.3 km.

summary.plain: A 3.3-kilometre ring that accelerates protons to 120 billion electronvolts. Its beam makes the NuMI neutrinos today and will make the LBNF beam for DUNE.
summary.technical: 3.3 km circumference proton synchrotron, design energy 150 GeV, operated at 120 GeV for neutrino production; slip-stacked Booster batches are loaded via the Recycler. Source of the NuMI beam and of the future LBNF beam.
